proposal.mixer_type: Static Mixer (Tee junction with inline static mixer)
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Gas and liquid are mixed immediately before the reactor inlet to ensure high interfacial area for mass transfer into the liquid phase surrounding the catalyst particles. The high pressure (10 bar) ensures significant hydrogen solubility in ethanol.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas ethanol solvent to remove dissolved oxygen.
Pre-heat liquid stream to 50 C using a heating coil.
Mix H2 gas and liquid stream via static mixer.
Pass through a pre-heater zone to ensure thermal equilibrium at 50 C before entering the packed bed.
post_reactor_steps: Pass through a gas-liquid separator (membrane or gravity-based) to remove unreacted H2.
Pass through a back-pressure regulator (BPR) set to 10 bar to maintain reactor pressure.
Cool product stream to ambient temperature.
Collect product or send to inline analysis (GC/HPLC).
proposal.chemistry_notes: Hydrogenation of alkenes on Pd/C is exothermic. In continuous flow, heat removal is efficient due to high surface-to-volume ratio. The residence time is kept identical to batch (4 h) to ensure complete conversion, assuming similar kinetics. The gas flow is set to 5 equivalents relative to the alkene to ensure excess hydrogen availability, though in practice, a slight excess is maintained continuously. The actual gas volume in the channel is calculated using the Ideal Gas Law at 10 bar and 50 C.

safety_flags: Hydrogen is flammable and explosive. Ensure all connections are leak-tight.
Pd/C is pyrophoric when dry. Keep catalyst wet with solvent.
High pressure (10 bar) requires rated equipment.
Exothermic reaction: monitor temperature closely to prevent runaway.
